newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia NSW National leader reaffirms Wik stance.
newsitem.headline: Australia NSW National leader reaffirms Wik stance.

text.p: Australia's New South Wales (NSW) state National party leader Ian Hunt said on Friday farmers would only be protected by extinguishment of native land rights on pastoral leases.
"The NSW National Party believes the rights of pastoral leaseholders in NSW will only be protected by extinguishing Native Title on pastoral leases," Hunt said in a statement.
"This is the only way to give pastoral leaseholders the certainty and security they had before the High Court's Wik case," he said.

Prime Minister John Howard is under pressure from farm groups and the National Party, the junior partner in his Liberal-National coalition, to abolish Aboriginal rights to government land leased to farmers.
The High Court ruled in favour of the Wik Aboriginal people in December, sparking a rerun of Australia's 1993 national debate over how to handle land claims without damaging the economy.
Howard has proposed a compromise confirming farmers' rights, but guaranteeing Aborigines limited access for traditional purposes.
Farmers and miners say uncertainty over what rights they have and what rights they might have in the future has damaged their multi-billion industries.
